mechanism_narrative: Sustained week-on-week improvement in RETAIL_REC (from -56.6% to -50.3% over four weeks) indicates a monotonic recovery trajectory. This trend will continue linearly over the next four weeks, producing higher mean RETAIL_REC than the baseline period.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 6.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses direction for two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Residential mobility remains elevated (20.0% above baseline) while retail remains depressed, indicating people are home-based. If RESIDENTIAL begins to decline toward baseline, displaced time will redirect to retail and recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL remains above 18% and RETAIL_REC does not increase by more than 3 percentage points within two weeks of the trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has plateaued at -72.3% (minimal week-on-week change from -73.7%), signaling stalled commuting recovery. If TRANSIT remains flat or worsens, workplace-based retail (lunch, after-work shopping) will not recover, constraining RETAIL_REC growth over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT change week-on-week is less than 1 percentage point in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT -73.7% to -72.3% (1.4 point improvement over 4 weeks)
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 percentage points within the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 5 percentage points despite TRANSIT stagnation.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered sharply (from -55.9% to -25.0%, a 30.9 point gain), indicating outdoor recreation substitution is active. This substitution effect will persist, crowding out indoor retail-and-recreation venues, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved 30.9 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: PARKS mobility reverses and falls below -35%, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 8 percentage points despite PARKS remaining above -30%.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized near -18% (minimal change from -18.9% to -18.3%), indicating essential shopping is locked in. Coupled with RETAIL_REC stagnation, this signals behavioral compartmentalization: consumers are not expanding discretionary retail trips. RETAIL_REC will remain depressed unless GROCERY_PHARM rises, indicating broader mobility normalization.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -15% while RETAIL_REC remains below -45%, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 6 percentage points within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved incrementally (from -45.4% to -41.3%, a 4.1 point gain over four weeks) but remains severely depressed. If WORKPLACES crosses -40% and continues rising, it signals policy-driven reopening of offices. This will trigger commuting-linked retail recovery, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -41.3%, improved 4.1 points over four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES does not sustain above -40% for two consecutive weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 4 percentage points within four weeks of WORKPLACES crossing -40%.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are co-dependent: commuting recovery requires both. Currently both are severely depressed and improving slowly. Only if TRANSIT improves by >3 points AND WORKPLACES improves by >3 points simultaneously will retail-linked commuting resume, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by >3 percentage points week-on-week
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or WORKPLACES fails to improve by >3 points in the same week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 5 percentage points within four weeks of the trigger condition being met.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility is declining gradually (from 23.4% to 20.0% over four weeks), indicating seasonal normalization of home time. As RESIDENTIAL continues to decline toward baseline over the next four weeks, outdoor and retail mobility will increase proportionally, lifting RETAIL_REC by 3-5 percentage points.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines by >0.5 percentage points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 3.4 points over four weeks from 23.4% to 20.0%
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL stabilizes or increases above 20%, or RETAIL_REC does not increase by at least 2 percentage points within four weeks despite RESIDENTIAL declining.
